challenge.better_approach: Looked: (a) a Stop hook committing dirty records, rejected: it would commit another ticket's records, the defect d3b8cdf81a41 just fixed in close.sh; (b) the ground loop, rejected: reaching for daemons is drift. A path-limited commit by the crossing verb's own caller is smallest.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every uncommitted crossing came through a verb (sail cross/verdict) rather than a close that failed midway: measured only for the three FIXME and one SUPERSEDED crossings I know; the 7cae18f7f9c2 BUILDME crossing's path is unread.
challenge.prior_art: In-house: close.sh commit_all (commits house tree with git add -u, commons via commons_paths.py); d3b8cdf81a41 (close commits only its own ticket's records); 11cd253f10bc/12443bcc113f (a PROVEME crossing refuses on dirty trees, but only at PROVEME); 09b1565a2045 (the lab's same shape, uncommitted derived copy). Grepped tickets for crossing-history-commit: no ticket owns crossing records committed at the verb.
challenge.real_collision: Possible with 12443bcc113f (another ticket's records do not refuse a crossing): committing own records at the verb is consistent with it; no Law contradicted. Distinction recorded.

answers.falsifier: After sail.py cross or sail.py verdict returns, git status of the crossing's component history.json and state.json is clean (committed, path-limited), verified by a proof that runs a scratch crossing; the five 2026-11-19 crossings could not have stayed dirty.
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a measured gap: five crossings of 2026-11-19 sat uncommitted in the akiendell house tree until akiendell-1eee-fixme-record (0065e73b6); see cairn/devices/cc/scripts/close.sh
answers.how: First-cut, a hypothesis: close.sh commits records only at close/prove, and sail.py cross and sail.py verdict commit nothing; make the crossing door's caller (sail cross/verdict) commit the crossing's own component history and state path-limited, or add a check that reds a crossing's records left dirty after the verb returns. The build chooses, measured.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (permanent in records of truth: a crossing that exists on one disk is not permanent); Law 4 (enforced by physics, not by a hand remembering sail step 10); Law 5 (the repo is itself the state of the machine).
answers.what: A crossing's history.json and state.json are committed by something that fires on every crossing, not only on a close, so a record of truth never exists on one disk alone.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-19 akiendell: five crossings sat only as uncommitted dirt in the house tree: tester seq 408 (1eeeab70c59e PROVEME->FIXME), codemother seq 172 (35bb99574043 PROVEME->FIXME), verdict seq 32 (8e0cfb77827c PROVEME->FIXME), chart_gate seq 9 (7cae18f7f9c2 TICKETME->BUILDME), seq 10 (c1a7130fba84 TICKETME->SUPERSEDED). Landed by hand on akiendell-1eee-fixme-record.

Read: projector.append_entry writes history/state and runs no git; no Stop/PostToolUse hook commits; close.sh commit_all is the only committer and runs at close/prove, which a verdict refusal or a supersede never reaches.
